hypothesis: A founder-led, agent-assisted licensor can operate a production Unbound for <=$0.5M/yr cash before scale
falsifier: Measured run cost >$0.8M/yr over the first 12 live months, or a partner/procurement demand forcing >=2 hires
test: Bottom-up quotes (insurance, SOC 2, pen test) at a term sheet; 12-month cost ledger

hypothesis: A channel partner will carry first-line support and procurement credibility so vendor support stays <=0.5 FTE
falsifier: Partner term sheet requires vendor 24x7 SLA or dedicated vendor staff
test: V-6 term-sheet terms

hypothesis: Partners and their customers accept a single-founder vendor with escrow, contracted second maintainer and adequate insurance
falsifier: >=2 of 5 partners cite vendor viability as disqualifying
test: V-6 conversations with a pre-registered viability question

hypothesis: Reusable onboarding packages (S6) cut implementation from ~$75k to ~$30k per sponsor
falsifier: Second implementation takes >=75% of first implementation hours
test: Hours ledger across the first two implementations

hypothesis: Founder-led structured interviews yield the same V-1 decision as paid third-party interviews
falsifier: Independent coder disagreement >20% on decisive-factor classification
test: Double coding of recorded V-1 interviews

hypothesis: Prices stated in interviews predict nonbinding EOI prices within 25%
falsifier: EOI prices below 75% of stated prices for >=2 of 3 respondents
test: V-2 at the $10k tier

hypothesis: Education and health foundations (>= $100M, no DAF) would launch a branded DAF programme if a host or licensed platform removed sponsor-level fixed cost
falsifier: Public-record review finds fewer than ~2 new institutional programmes a year in 2021-26, or V-1 interviews show institutions prefer referring donors to national sponsors
test: $0: scan 990 Part IV line 6 and Schedule D changes FY2021-25 for first-time institutional filers; programme-page review; then V-1 interviews

hypothesis: An existing sponsor will license a separate platform to host other institutions' programmes without moving its main book
falsifier: Hosts require a single system for all funds (S4 becomes a displacement sale)
test: V-6 partner conversations with 3-5 host-capable sponsors (after authorization)

hypothesis: CU league foundations running institutional DAFs have manual back-office pain they would pay to remove
falsifier: League fee pages and 990s show outsourced administration or adequate staffing; or no willingness to pay
test: $0: 990 Part VII-B contractor lines and staffing for the 4+ league foundations; later V-2

hypothesis: Narrow component offerings (charity intelligence, migration assessment) convert to platform licences within 24 months at a meaningful rate
falsifier: Fewer than 1 in 10 narrow-offering customers enter platform evaluation within 24 months
test: Instrument any narrow pilot; analogous-vendor case review

hypothesis: Per-programme acquisition plus onboarding cost can be held below one year of programme licence revenue through a host sponsor or league channel
falsifier: Measured CAC+onboarding per hosted programme exceeds annual licence revenue for the first 5 programmes
test: Track first host's programme pipeline (G1+)

hypothesis: Loss of a host sponsor (e.g. BNY Mellon CGF Dec 2024) creates programme-replacement demand
falsifier: Affected programmes moved to another existing sponsor without evaluation, or were closed
test: $0: trace where GW and MSU programmes moved (990s, pages)

hypothesis: Kill-rule trigger claim: if no channel partner or design-partner customer reaches term-sheet talks within six months of a funded partner search, the partner route is unavailable rather than slow
falsifier: At month 6 two or more partners are in active diligence with a stated decision date and at least one signs by month 12
test: Log every V-6 contact with stage and date from the first approved conversation; review at cost-center month + 6

hypothesis: At least ~10 sponsors large enough to pay ER-7 revenue per customer (>=2,646 accounts) are reachable through a channel partner without displacing a contracted incumbent, or a partner will license Unbound for its aggregated book at ER-7-scale revenue
falsifier: Desk classification and V-6 show fewer than ~10 such sponsors outside captive or contracted platforms and no partner offering aggregated-book economics
test: P3-VAL-CE001 desk classification ($0); V-6 conversations

hypothesis: Compliance-led sponsor buyers will pay at least ~$10 per account-year more (or choose Unbound at price parity) for replayable, provenance-bound eligibility decisions
falsifier: Auditors and compliance officers in V-3 rate replay as no better than a Candid Charity Check report plus an audit log
test: V-3 auditor walkthrough on the public-data replay harness; no spend

hypothesis: Incumbents will not respond specifically to a partner-delivered Unbound module for 12-24 months because it is below their attention threshold
falsifier: An incumbent discounts, matches commitments or pre-empts renewal at the first competitive evaluation
test: Observe the first partner pilot evaluation; ask the partner what the incumbent offered

hypothesis: Ren's rational response to a lost or threatened account is price concession and contract extension at renewal, not product change
falsifier: Ren ships a replay or migration-outcome feature aimed at the threat within 12 months
test: Win/loss interviews with stayers (V-1) asking what the incumbent offered at renewal

hypothesis: Continuous control evidence lowers the licensor's SOC 1/SOC 2/Nacha TPSP audit cost by 25% or more versus conventional evidence collection
falsifier: CPA scoping quote is unchanged by the evidence architecture
test: Ask a CPA firm for a scoping view of the design at no cost (no engagement)

hypothesis: Multi-lineage incumbents (DFX, iPhi CoreEnterprise, Pinkaloo lineage) cannot offer bitemporal replay across all books within 18 months (W06)
falsifier: Ren publicly documents a unified ledger with point-in-time replay, or a buyer reports it in an evaluation
test: Monitor Ren release notes and RFP feedback

hypothesis: A channel partner will accept a non-exclusive licence with change-of-control termination and data-continuity terms
falsifier: Every partner conversation demands exclusivity or acquisition (CLM-025)
test: V-6 distributor conversations

hypothesis: A planned-giving (gift annuity, CRT, pooled income fund) administration module can reuse at least 60% of Unbound ledger, control, payment and tax-reporting components
falsifier: Requirement mapping shows that actuarial valuation, beneficiary payout, trust tax returns and state reserve reporting need more new domain objects than reused ones
test: $0 desk mapping of public PG Calc service scope, IRS Form 5227/1099-R/K-1 obligations and NY/CA reserve filings against Unbound requirement IDs

hypothesis: Comprehensive (Model A) fiscal sponsors would pay for project sub-fund accounting with restricted balances, disbursement controls and payee vetting built on Unbound components
falsifier: Public field-scan pain points are dominated by legal/HR services rather than accounting software; or price tolerance is below ~$5k a year
test: Read the 2023 field scan and 2025 state-of-field results ($0); later a V-2-style price question to 5 sponsors

hypothesis: Publishing commercial licence terms for released developer components (Strata, Limen, Forma/Folio, Aegis) yields at least 5 paying commercial licensees within 12 months without a sales effort
falsifier: Fewer than 5 commercial licences (or zero inbound requests) 12 months after terms are public
test: Publish terms; count inbound requests and licences; record support hours per licensee

hypothesis: A channel partner sources at least one qualified sponsor per year after enablement, with a sales cycle no longer than direct (6-24 months)
falsifier: No partner-sourced qualified opportunity within 12 months of a signed partner agreement
test: Track partner-sourced opportunities from V-6 onward; compare cycle length

hypothesis: An embedded DAF module partner will accept a capped, declining revenue share of 15-30% with non-exclusivity and Echelon direct-reference rights
falsifier: Every engaged partner requires >40% share, exclusivity, or acquisition/ROFR terms (CHL-084)
test: Term-sheet conversations under V-6 (no commitments under BRIEF constraints)

hypothesis: Public, reproducible evidence (open repositories, published research, deterministic demos) shortens partner technical diligence
falsifier: Partners still require the same SOC 2 Type 2 history and vendor-viability review regardless of public evidence
test: Ask in V-6 conversations which diligence items public evidence satisfied

hypothesis: Employee-giving and CSR platforms (beyond DAF sponsors) would buy provenance-bound charity eligibility evidence at >= $15k a year (extends HYP-007)
falsifier: None of 3-5 such platforms states a gap that Candid or in-house vetting does not already fill
test: Desk review of public vetting statements; include in V-8 sample

hypothesis: Human-relevant eligibility change rate among in-use charities is <=1% a year (vs 4% HYP-006)
falsifier: 12-release replay shows >2% of Schedule I recipients with adverse eligibility-relevant changes needing a person
test: Archive monthly IRS releases; replay against parsed Schedule I recipients (P3-VAL-HI001)

hypothesis: Automated 180-day renewal fails for <=1% of tier-1 charities and <=10% of tier-2
falsifier: Simulated renewals on archived releases and roster retrieval fail above those rates
test: Replay renewal logic on archived releases; test automated roster retrieval for top GENs (P3-VAL-HI003)

hypothesis: Federal bulk connectors need <=30 engineering hours per connector-year
falsifier: Desk reconstruction finds more than ~2 breaking format/schema changes per source-year
test: P3-VAL-HI004

hypothesis: No buyer category will pay >=$15k a year for a standalone charity eligibility evidence service
falsifier: V-8 finds >=3 of 10 at >=$15k
test: Desk price survey now; V-8 later when outreach is authorised

hypothesis: A structured contribution intent eliminates >=50% of attribution investigations without net donor effort where it replaces existing notification forms
falsifier: Pilot shows orphans unchanged or donor abandonment
test: Synthetic replay of memo/FBO carry-through; design-partner measurement later

hypothesis: Government units and school districts (~0.5% of Schedule I rows) can be verified deterministically from Census of Governments and NCES CCD
falsifier: Name/address matching to those lists cannot reach >=90% precision
test: Extend replay harness with Census/NCES joins (P3-VAL-HI005)

hypothesis: Registry overlap exponent across sponsors is <=0.5
falsifier: Schedule I recipient union across 20 sponsors grows faster than N*S^0.5
test: Compute union growth from replay data (P3-VAL-HI002)
